newsitem.title: USA: Mount McKinley has first death of climbing season.
newsitem.headline: Mount McKinley has first death of climbing season.

text.p: A climber fell and died during his descent of Mount McKinley, the National Park Service said on Friday, becoming the first casualty this season on North America's tallest peak.
The victim's name was not released, but he was part of a four-man party from outside the United States.

The fall occurred after two members of the party reached McKinley's 20,320-foot (6,194-metre) summit late on Thursday and were trying to return to a camp at 17,000 feet (5,200 metres) where their companions were waiting, said Park Service spokesman John Quinley.
The pair took a short fall on a steep gully known as the Messner Couloir, Quinley said. Instead of going back up to the top of the couloir, they launched a traverse across it, he said.
In the whiteout conditions, the pair overshot their camp. Roped together, they fell again, a distance that rangers estimated was about 500 feet (150 metres).
One of the climbers was knocked unconscious by the fall, Quinley said. "When he came around, the other guy was on top of him, and dead," he said.
The survivor, yelling and crawling, was rescued by another climber along the well-travelled West Buttress route.
Rangers believe the fall occurred at about midnight, Quinley said, adding that rescuers were waiting for the weather to improve before retrieving the body.
